record.nameMeaning: "Meat-eating bull", for its bull-like brow horns
record.oneLiner: A horned, tiny-armed abelisaurid predator of Cretaceous South America.
record.description: Carnotaurus was a lightly built bipedal predator from the Late Cretaceous of Argentina, 7.5–8 m long. It is unique among carnivorous dinosaurs in having two thick horns above its eyes, on a deep skull and muscular neck. It had extremely small, vestigial forelimbs and long, slender legs, and its skin is preserved as a mosaic of small scales.

notableFacts.text: The only carnivorous dinosaur with two thick brow horns.
Had extremely small, vestigial forelimbs — even shorter than T. rex's.
Known from extensive skin impressions of small, non-overlapping scales.
